coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Rock Block J
record.summary: A flex block on Channel Lane and Terry A. Francois Boulevard one row north of Block I, developable as commercial (90 ft) or residential (120 ft). No source read shows construction on it (the Port's June 2026 report: Phase 2, not yet begun, could start construction as early as 2027); the EIR's illustrative schedule had it in the last construction area.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt block): no Assessor lot of its own yet. It sits on lot 8719A006, the ~37,400 m2 undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 that also holds Blocks C, D, E, H, I, J, Mission Rock Square, Channel Lane and the unbuilt internal streets. Traced 2026-09-17 from the adopted Design Controls' Figure 6.2 through a transform with 0.7 m RMS residual on 16 real lot corners, with vertices snapped to recorded lot lines where the figure draws the block against one (see digitization_method): treat street-facing and lot-line edges as accurate to ~1 m and interior edges (against unbuilt streets and open spaces) to ~1-3 m. The block's shape is the Design Controls' block, not a building footprint; a building may sit back from these lines.
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls (Port of San Francisco, document dated April 24, 2018), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151); land use from Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); block corners snapped to the recorded DataSF Assessor lot lines of the 2020 Seawall Lot 337 subdivision where they fall within 3 m.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this block -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so joining status.csv to it would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this block touches them.
notes.regulatory_context: Flex block (Residential MU or Commercial MU), max height 90 ft commercial / 120 ft residential. Sits one row north of Block I, adjacent to Block F -- it does NOT front Mission Rock Square directly, despite some secondary summaries grouping it with the square's surrounding blocks.

The Port's October 2023 report records that the developer sent the Phase 2 Submittal on December 28, 2022, that Phase 2 was 'not currently financially feasible' and that work on it was decelerated, and models a 'hypothetical Phase 2 start date of March 2026' for illustration. The Port's June 5, 2026 report asks the Commission to approve up to $10 million of pre-development funding to accelerate Phase 2 (Resolution 26-34), with construction possible 'as early as 2027'. Neither report lists which blocks Phase 2 includes.

changes.text: Corrections to Block J: the Design Controls are now called a document dated April 24, 2018. The base-building height fact now gives 60 ft with a 40 ft maximum along the Terry A. Francois Boulevard side, not 40 ft alone. The phase-status fact no longer presents the 2023 deceleration as the current state; it adds the June 2026 request to accelerate Phase 2. The Design Controls approval milestone now cites the Sept 2019 Port memo that gives the Jan 30, 2018 date and notes the memo numbers that resolution 18-05 while the January 26 staff report requested it as 18-04. The Board of Supervisors milestone no longer names 'Resolution 33-18' (the Port's reports call it a resolution and an ordinance; the Notice of Determination gives File No. 171286). The Oct 2023 milestone now says Port and developer staff agreed earlier in 2023 to decelerate Phase 2 and that Resolution 23-46's recitals state it, rather than a Commission finding on Oct 10; the March 2025 milestone quotes the memo's words and calls the 132 BMR-unit cut a proposal. The Draft EIR phasing milestone no longer says it was 'superseded'; it cites the Port's Oct 2023 list of Phase 1 buildings. The D4D source is retitled the March 2012 Design + Development Revised Proposal by the Giants and The Cordish Companies (a developer proposal, not the Design for Development), the Design Controls source is credited to the Port only, and the Design Controls figure credit no longer names Mission Rock Partners or an adoption date. The map notes now say no source read shows construction on the block and cite the Port's June 2026 report instead of a bare 'unbuilt'; the 'within 3%' area claim is corrected in a new dated note (lot A is about 3.3% under the 2012 table).

open_questions: Whether Block J will be built residential or commercial has not been decided in any document read.

No construction start, Phase 2 budget approval or vertical design submittal for this block was found in Port Commission agendas through February 2026; the block remains part of the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot (Lot A).
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.
The DDA 'Outside Dates' for commencing later phases are in the DDA itself, which was not read.
No cost, developer capital or land-value figure exists for this block; the Port says Phase 2 appraisals are deferred until the market supports the minimum land values.

Images: no rendering specific to this block exists in the public-record documents read (the Design Controls give only diagrammatic envelopes), and the 2026 aerial serves as the 'before'/'now' view of the parking lot it sits in.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Block J. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. The DDA itself (lodged with the Board of Supervisors 2/1/2018, Board File 180092, adopted as Resolution 42-18, effective 8/15/2018) places Parcel J in Phase 4 in its Land Use Table (DDA Section 1.5) and its Exhibit B2 Schedule of Performance gives a 2018 'Target Date' of February 2025 for completing Phase 4's horizontal Phase Improvements -- already elapsed with the earlier Phase 2 still not begun as of the October 2023 'not currently financially feasible' finding in this record's own milestones. No later Port memo, Design Controls revision or news source gives a revised target year for Phase 4 or for the Project's full buildout, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports a non-elapsed date for this block.

The Design Controls approval is numbered Resolution 18-04 in the Port's January 26, 2018 staff report (a request) and Resolution 18-05 in its September 20, 2019 memo; the adopted resolution itself was not read.
Which blocks Phase 2 covers is not stated in the Port's June 5, 2026 report either, so this block's phase is not sourced from it.
